title: Recall Quiz: Contemporary Age: Larkin, Heaney, Orwell, Golding, Rushdie, Naipaul

questions.q: The famous line 'All animals are equal, but some animals are more equal than others' appears in which work?
questions.explanation: This is the ultimate corrupted commandment in Orwell's 'Animal Farm'.

questions.q: George Orwell's novel '1984', which introduced concepts like 'Big Brother' and 'Thought Police', belongs to which literary genre?
questions.explanation: A dystopia is an imagined state or society in which there is great suffering or injustice, typically totalitarian.

questions.q: William Golding's 'Lord of the Flies' primarily argues that:
options: Children are inherently pure and innocent.
British culture is superior to others.
There is an inherent darkness and savagery in human nature.
Proper education can solve all social problems.
questions.explanation: The boys quickly shed civilization and resort to murder, proving humanity's inherent darkness.

questions.q: Philip Larkin was a leading figure of which 1950s British poetry group that favored colloquial language and traditional forms over Modernist complexity?
questions.explanation: Larkin and 'The Movement' reacted against the excesses of Dylan Thomas and T.S. Eliot.

questions.q: Which novel by Salman Rushdie uses 'Magic Realism' to tell the story of children born at the exact moment of India's independence?
questions.explanation: Midnight's Children links the protagonist Saleem Sinai's life directly to the history of India.

questions.q: The literary style that seamlessly blends fantastical or magical elements with an otherwise realistic, mundane environment is known as:
questions.explanation: Magic Realism is heavily associated with Salman Rushdie and Latin American authors.

questions.q: Which post-colonial author, born in Trinidad to Indian descendants, wrote 'A House for Mr Biswas'?
questions.explanation: Naipaul's works often deal with alienation and the lingering effects of colonialism.

questions.q: Seamus Heaney, the Nobel Prize-winning poet famous for his poems about bogs and rural landscapes, is from which country?
questions.explanation: Heaney is one of Ireland's greatest modern poets.
